name: Satyapala
occupation: Head Forester / Royal Boundary-Keeper of the Reserve Forest (Aranyapala)
residence: Edge of the Shalavana (Sal Forest), near the royal timber yards outside Pataliputra's palisade
personality: suspicious of outsiders and soft thinking
loyal to trusted people and cold to others
daily_routine: patrolling the boundary pillars marking the royal reserve forest from village land
issuing and checking felling permits for sal timber bound for palisade repair and river ships
checking tree health and marking safe cutting zones
escorting timber workers into the deeper reserve sections
tracking elephant herds and reporting to the royal elephant corps' surveyors
monitoring flood-prone riverbank groves during the monsoon
reporting unusual forest conditions to the Gramika
delivering timber quotas to the royal carpentry yards and the market plaza

goals.public_goal: Enforce the King's forest law, keep the reserve sal groves and elephant tracts safe from illegal felling and hunting, and ensure timber reaches Pataliputra's workshops and palisade repairs without accident
goals.hidden_goal: Track how the royal boundary pillars have quietly drifted over the years as new farmland is cleared into the reserve
goals.deep_goal: Understand why certain groves in the reserve feel 'wrong' even when nothing about them looks out of place

beliefs: The reserve forest is not fully mapped, even now, whatever the boundary pillars claim
Sal trees do not grow in straight rows by accident
Some felling paths disappear faster than regrowth explains
The old warnings passed down from forest-keepers before him are usually rooted in something real
The city assumes the forest is settled and known, when it isn't
